drug_class: CNS Agent / Sigma-1 Receptor Agonist combined with CYP2D6 Inhibitor
purpose: This medication is used to treat a condition called Pseudobulbar Affect, or PBA. PBA causes sudden, uncontrollable episodes of laughing or crying that do not match how you actually feel inside. It often affects people with neurological conditions like ALS or multiple sclerosis.
how_it_works: Dextromethorphan works in your brain to help control the nerve signals that trigger those uncontrollable laughing or crying episodes. However, your body breaks down dextromethorphan too quickly on its own, so quinidine is added to slow that process down. Together, they allow enough dextromethorphan to stay in your system long enough to actually work.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, dizziness, cough, vomiting, weakness, and swelling in your legs or feet. Some people also feel tired or have an upset stomach. Tell your doctor if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medication can affect your heart rhythm, so it is not recommended if you have certain heart conditions. It can interact with many other medications, especially antidepressants, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist everything you are taking. Do not take it if you are also taking MAO inhibitors, as this can be very dangerous. It may also cause dizziness, so be careful when standing up or driving.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one capsule (20 mg dextromethorphan / 10 mg quinidine) taken by mouth once daily for 7 days. After that, the dose typically increases to one capsule twice a day, taken about 12 hours apart. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
